title: Rivetus and Moulin: assent plus particular fiducia — adoption’s inward witness
source_text: IX. Eadem est quoque descriptio Riveti olim in Academia Leydensi Sacrae Theologiae Professoris celeberrimi: Salvificam, inquit, illam & justificantem fidem dicimus, ex certa revelationis divinae notitia, firmum a Spiritu Sancto per verbum Evangelii animis nostris ingeneratum assensum, omnibus quae nobis Deus in verbo suo patefecit, sed praesertim salutaribus in Christo promissionibus, quo certa fiducia in Deo acquiescens, unusquisque fidelis firmiter statuit, non solum in genere promissam esse credentibus remissionem peccatorum, sed sibi in particulari concessam, aeternamque justitiam, & ex ea vitam, Dei misericordia, propter unius Domini Jesu Christi meritum donatam esse. Similiter Petrus Moulinus, celeberrimus etiam, dum Disputatione viveret, in Academia Sedanensi Professor, idem definit esse Firmum assensum promissionibus Evangelii, quo fidelis non tantum credit eas esse veras, sed etiam ad se particulariter pertinere, spiritu adoptionis testimonium intrinsecus perhibente eum esse filium Dei; unde pax conscientiae, & fiducia, & opera charitatis. Thesibus de Justificatione & Fide justificante, parte 2. Thesi 12.
pass_a_gloss: The same also is the description of Rivetus, formerly most celebrated Professor of Sacred Theology in the Academy of Leiden: That saving and justifying faith, he says, we call a firm assent generated in our minds by the Holy Spirit through the word of the Gospel from a sure knowledge of the divine revelation, to all things which God has disclosed to us in His word, but especially to the saving promises in Christ, by which, resting in God with sure trust, each of the faithful firmly lays down that remission of sins is promised to believers not only in general, but granted to himself in particular, and that eternal justice, and life from it, have been given by God’s mercy for the merit of the one Lord Jesus Christ. Likewise Peter du Moulin, also most celebrated while he lived, Professor in the Academy of Sedan, defines the same to be a Firm assent to the promises of the Gospel, by which the faithful not only believes them to be true, but also that they belong particularly to himself, the spirit of adoption inwardly bearing witness that he is a son of God; whence peace of conscience, and trust, and works of charity. Theses on Justification and Justifying Faith, part 2, Thesis 12.
pass_b_english: Rivetus: Spirit-wrought firm assent to revealed things — especially saving promises in Christ.
Fiducia rests in God: remission not only in general but mine; eternal justice and life for Christ’s merit.
Du Moulin (Sedan): firm assent that Gospel promises are true and particularly mine.
Spirit of adoption inwardly witnesses sonship → peace, trust, charity’s works.
